$comment: Shape documentation only. The live set is supplied at composition time by
the COMPOSITION_EXTENSIONS repository secret, so the host builds and runs
identically with a different set or with none, and adding an extension
never edits the host. A list committed here would make this file the thing
that has to change, which is the coupling the secret exists to avoid.
'repository' and 'workflow' are the trust declaration: the host verifies
each signature against the identity built from them, so an extension cannot
widen who may sign for it by editing its own repository. Listing an
extension grants nothing on its own; each is still admitted independently,
and the host refuses to boot unless the lock inventory exactly matches the
enabled set.
An empty 'extensions' list composes the host with none; a missing one fails.
'retired' lists the ids of extensions taken out on purpose. A deploy refuses
an image that drops an extension production runs unless the image's
composition names it here, so an extension leaves production only by being
named. An id cannot be both listed and retired. Once production runs
without it, the entry may go.
Several entries may name one repository: one repository is one trust
domain, so they name the same workflow, and each id is read from that
repository's admission run as its own artifact, admission-<id>. Optional
'path' is the entry's package directory inside its repository, '.' when
omitted; a coordinated branch builds the extension from there.
Example:
{ "extensions": [ { "id": "example.alpha",
"repository": "owner/example-alpha",
"workflow": ".github/workflows/admit-plugin.yml",
"path": "packages/example-alpha" } ],
"retired": [ "example.beta" ] }
